    "slug": "layout/breakpoints",

    "title": "Breakpoints",
    "description": "Build mobile-first layouts with viewport queries and opt-in container queries.",
    "lead": "Build mobile-first layouts with viewport queries and opt-in container queries.",
    "sections": [
      {
        "heading": "Core concepts",
        "paragraphs": [
          "Start with styles that work at the narrowest width, then add changes as space becomes available. Viewport breakpoints measure the browser window. Container queries measure an eligible ancestor, so the same component can adapt differently in a sidebar and a main column."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Available breakpoints",
        "table": {
          "headings": [
            "Tier",
            "Minimum",
            "Prefix"
          ],
          "rows": [
            [
              "xs",
              "0",
              "none"
            ],
            [
              "sm",

            ],
            [
              "md",
              "768px",
              "md:"
            ],
            [
              "lg",
              "1024px",
              "lg:"
            ],
            [
              "xl",
              "1280px",
              "xl:"
            ],
            [
              "2xl",
              "1536px",
              "2xl:"
            ]
          ]
        },
        "paragraphs": [
          "The default Sass map has six keys, with numeric/unit key 2xl, not a duplicate xxl alias. Responsive Flexbox classes use viewport prefixes; CSS Grid placement uses container prefixes. Infix and legacy cq-* names are not emitted."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Media queries",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "scss",
            "source": "@use 'tremplin/scss/layout/breakpoints' as bp;\n.dashboard { display: grid; }\n@include bp.media-breakpoint-up(lg) {\n  .dashboard { grid-template-columns: 18rem 1fr; }\n}"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "Range queries use inclusive lower bounds and exclusive upper bounds. There is no .02px subtraction or media-up convenience alias."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Max-width",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "scss",
            "source": "@use 'tremplin/scss/layout/breakpoints' as bp;\n@include bp.media-breakpoint-down(md) { .project-navigation { flex-direction: column; } }"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "down(md) means width < 768px, not the whole md tier. Zero/null upper bounds emit unqueried content; down(xs) is unconditional. A typo can yield a null bound rather than a useful range."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Single breakpoint",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "scss",
            "source": "@use 'tremplin/scss/layout/breakpoints' as bp;\n@include bp.media-breakpoint-only(md) { .project-panel { width: 40rem; } }"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "only(md) spans 768px &lt;= width &lt; 1024px; only(2xl) is unbounded above. Map order determines the next tier. Unknown keys are not coerced to aliases."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Between breakpoints",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "scss",
            "source": "@use 'tremplin/scss/layout/breakpoints' as bp;\n@include bp.media-breakpoint-between(md, xl) { .project-summary { display: grid; } }"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "between(md,xl) spans 768px &lt;= width &lt; 1280px. Null bounds are open. Reversed positive bounds are emitted as written, not sorted."
        ],
        "table": {
          "headings": [
            "Call",
            "Local default interval"
          ],
          "rows": [
            [
              "up(md)",
              "width >= 768px"
            ],
            [
              "down(md)",
              "width < 768px"
            ],
            [
              "only(md)",
              "768px &lt;= width &lt; 1024px"
            ],
            [
              "between(md, xl)",
              "768px &lt;= width &lt; 1280px"
            ]
          ]
        }
      },
      {
        "heading": "Custom breakpoints",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "scss",
            "source": "@use 'tremplin/scss/config' with (\n  $breakpoints: (base: 0, compact: 30rem, wide: 60rem),\n  $container-max-widths: (sm: null, md: null, lg: null, xl: null, 2xl: null, compact: 28rem, wide: 56rem)\n);\n@use 'tremplin/scss/tremplin-grid';"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "Breakpoints replace the entire map. Container maximums merge defaults; remove unmatched default keys explicitly. Unmatched maximum keys can emit an unqueried container maximum in the pin. Keep maps coherent and ordered."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Migration from previous defaults",
        "paragraphs": [
          "Strict core removes infix aliases, xxl aliases, separate legacy container-breakpoints and the container-widths configuration name. Migrate markup to canonical prefixes and configure container-max-widths. Do not load compatibility CSS into the strict bundle."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Canonical largest tier",
        "example": "<div class=\"row g-3\" data-layout-demo=\"largest-canonical\"><div class=\"col-12 2xl:col-6\"><div class=\"border rounded p-3\">Canonical 2xl</div></div><div class=\"col-12 2xl:col-6\"><div class=\"border rounded p-3\">Canonical 2xl</div></div></div>",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "html",
            "source": "<div class=\"row g-3\"><div class=\"col-12 2xl:col-6\">First</div><div class=\"col-12 2xl:col-6\">Second</div></div>"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "Only canonical 2xl is present by default. The generated selector escapes its leading digit; HTML keeps the literal 2xl:col-6 spelling. A custom xxl map key is an explicit independent tier, not an automatic alias. Use the actual Sass key type in lookups."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Container queries",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "html",
            "source": "<div class=\"grid\">\n  <article class=\"g-col-12 sm:g-col-6\">First</article>\n  <article class=\"g-col-12 sm:g-col-6\">Second</article>\n</div>"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "grid establishes inline-size containment. Its descendants use the shared breakpoint map: sm=576px, md=768px. The container cannot query itself; a nearer eligible ancestor changes which size is measured. There are no cq-span-* aliases."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Container query mixins",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "scss",
            "source": "@use 'tremplin/scss/layout/breakpoints' as bp;\n.project-frame { @include bp.set-container(inline-size, project-frame); }\n@include bp.container-breakpoint-between(sm, lg, project-frame) { .project-items { display: grid; } }\n@include bp.container-breakpoint-only(lg, project-frame) { .project-items { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; } }\n@include bp.container-breakpoint-down(sm, project-frame) { .project-items { display: block; } }"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "Container range mixins mirror viewport intervals, measuring an eligible named or nearest ancestor. Physical width is queried even in vertical writing. Size containment can affect intrinsic sizing; give shrink-to-fit layouts deliberate dimensions."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Named containers",
        "paragraphs": [
          "A named query selects an eligible ancestor with that name even when a nearer unnamed container exists. Use a matching name in set-container(inline-size, project-frame) and the query mixin. An absent matching ancestor means a bounded query does not apply; an unbounded branch emits ordinary CSS without requiring a container.",
          "The physical width feature uses width; it is not rewritten to inline-size in vertical writing modes. Relative em bounds resolve against the query container’s font size, unlike em media queries, which use the browser’s initial font size. Verify container padding, zoom, nesting, and RTL with real content."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Sass functions and loops",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "scss",
            "source": "@use 'tremplin/scss/layout/breakpoints' as bp;\n$tiers: (base: 0, compact: 30rem, wide: 60rem);\n@include bp.loop-breakpoints-up($tiers) using ($name, $prefix) {\n  @include bp.media-breakpoint-up($name, $tiers) { .#{$prefix}project-grid { display: grid; } }\n}"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "Functions include breakpoint-next/min/max/prefix and css-escape-ident. loop-breakpoints-up supplies name/prefix; down supplies current/next/next-prefix in ascending map order. loop-breakpoints is the pinned down-loop alias, not a reversed iteration. next/only require known keys; min/max/prefix can return null or an empty prefix for missing keys."
        ]
      }

        "paragraphs": [

        ],
        "paragraphs": [

          "g-* sets both axes, gx-* horizontal and gy-* vertical; responsive names use md:g-4/md:gx-4/md:gy-3. Gutters defaults to the spacer map: keys 0–12, g-3=.5rem, gx-4=.75rem. Base row gutters remain 1.5rem horizontal and 0 vertical."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "No gutters",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "html",
            "source": "<div class=\"row g-0\">\n  <div class=\"col-6\">First</div>\n  <div class=\"col-6\">Second</div>\n</div>"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "g-0 removes row gutters, not padding inside a card or the surrounding container. Do not replace it with gap-* on a fixed-width twelve-column Flexbox row: native gap adds space beyond column percentages and can force wrapping."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Change the gutters",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "scss",
            "source": "@use 'tremplin/scss' with (\n  $grid-gutter-x: 2rem,\n  $grid-gutter-y: .5rem,\n  $grid-row-columns: 4,\n  $gutters: (0: 0, 2: .5rem, 3: 1rem, wide: 2rem)\n);"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "Override --trm-gutter-x/y on rows locally. An explicit gutters map replaces the whole map; use valid lengths and omit unwanted keys. It does not change spacing utilities. Native CSS Grid gap uses --trm-gap with no legacy grid-gap fallback. Container padding, Flexbox gutters and Grid gap remain separate controls."
        ]
      }
    ],
    "reference": {title:'Tremplin source',url:'https://github.com/DevCiel/tremplin/blob/main/site/src/data/layout-guides.ts'}

          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Margin and padding",
        "paragraphs": [
          "Use m-* and p-* for every side, x/y for axes, and s/e for logical inline start/end. ms-auto absorbs available inline-start space. Use gap-* for ordinary Flexbox or CSS Grid composition; use gutter classes for the percentage-based row/column grid."
        ],
        "code": [

          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "The native visible/invisible utilities set visibility; invisible preserves geometry but hides content from normal focus/assistive interaction. They do not replace hidden/display semantics. See the Utility API for explicit custom variants."

    "slug": "layout/z-index",
    "group": "Layout",
    "title": "Z-index",
    "description": "Understand stacking contexts before changing the layer order of interface elements.",
    "lead": "Understand stacking contexts before changing the layer order of interface elements.",
    "sections": [
      {
        "heading": "Stacking order",
        "paragraphs": [
          "A z-index value is compared within a stacking context, not across the entire document. Positioning, transforms, opacity, isolation, and other properties can create new contexts. Increasing an arbitrary number may not bring a child above a sibling context."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Local scale",
        "table": {
          "headings": [
            "Map key",
            "Value"
          ],
          "rows": [
            [
              "n1 / 0 / 1 / 2 / 3",
              "-1 / 0 / 1 / 2 / 3"
            ],
            [
              "menu",
              "1000"
            ],
            [
              "sticky",
              "1010"
            ],
            [
              "fixed",
              "1020"
            ],
            [
              "drawer",
              "1030"
            ],
            [
              "dialog",
              "1040"
            ],
            [
              "popover",
              "1050"
            ],
            [
              "tooltip",
              "1060"
            ],
            [
              "toast",
              "1070"
            ]
          ]
        },
        "paragraphs": [
          "zindex-levels owns the shared z-* utilities and --trm-zindex-* tokens. No modal/offcanvas/dropdown/backdrop compatibility keys are added. Native top-layer order is separate from numeric z-index."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Native top layer",
        "paragraphs": [
          "Native modal dialogs and browser popovers can enter the browser’s top layer. Ordinary z-index values cannot place regular page content above a top-layer modal. Test Dialog, Drawer, Menu, Tooltip, and nested overlays together before changing their layer rules."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Sass configuration",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "scss",
            "source": "@use 'sass:map';\n@use 'tremplin/scss/config' as config with (\n  $zindex-levels: (n1: -1, 0: 0, 1: 1, 2: 2, 3: 3, menu: 1000, sticky: 1010, fixed: 1020, drawer: 1030, dialog: 1040, popover: 1050, tooltip: 1060, toast: 1070)\n);\n@use 'tremplin/scss';\n.project-tooltip { position: absolute; z-index: map.get(config.$zindex-levels, tooltip); }"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "This map is replaced, not merged by defaults(). Supply the full coherent scale when changing it. There is no z-index() convenience function; use map.get or the emitted root token."
        ]
      }

  {
    "slug": "layout/css-grid",
    "group": "Layout",
    "title": "CSS Grid",
    "description": "Use explicit column spans and native gaps for two-dimensional layouts.",
    "lead": "Use explicit column spans and native gaps for two-dimensional layouts.",
    "sections": [
      {
        "heading": "How it works",
        "paragraphs": [
          "CSS Grid is enabled by default in the Tremplin core. The grid class creates twelve 1fr tracks, one explicit 1fr row, a 1.5rem gap and an inline-size query container. These rules participate in the layout layer.",
          "Use g-col-N for a literal column span and g-start-N for a start line. Prefixes such as md:g-col-6 query the nearest eligible container, normally the grid, rather than the viewport. Native gap replaces Flexbox gutters and negative margins. Unclassified children use normal Grid auto-placement; there is no full-row child reset."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Examples",
        "example": "<div class=\"grid\" data-layout-demo=\"css-grid\"><div class=\"g-col-4 border rounded p-3\">First</div><div class=\"g-col-4 border rounded p-3\">Second</div><div class=\"g-col-4 border rounded p-3\">Third</div></div>",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "html",
            "source": "<div class=\"grid\">\n  <article class=\"g-col-4\">First</article>\n  <article class=\"g-col-4\">Second</article>\n  <article class=\"g-col-4\">Third</article>\n</div>"
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Container-responsive spans",
        "example": "<div class=\"grid\" data-layout-demo=\"modern-query\" style=\"resize:horizontal;overflow:auto;min-inline-size:12rem;max-inline-size:100%\"><div class=\"g-col-12 sm:g-col-6 border rounded p-3\">First</div><div class=\"g-col-12 sm:g-col-6 border rounded p-3\">Second</div></div>",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "html",
            "source": "<div class=\"grid\">\n  <article class=\"g-col-12 sm:g-col-6\">First</article>\n  <article class=\"g-col-12 sm:g-col-6\">Second</article>\n</div>"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "Resize the grid: these items become half-width at the default sm container minimum of 576px. md uses 768px. Only prefix-style responsive classes are generated. Changing the viewport alone does not cross a container threshold when the grid width stays fixed.",
          "A responsive-only item such as md:g-col-6 auto-places in one track below md. Add g-col-12 if it must start full-width. A nearer nested query container changes which ancestor is measured."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Starts and wrapping",
        "example": "<div class=\"grid\"><div class=\"g-col-6 g-start-4 border rounded p-3\">Six tracks, starting at line four</div></div>",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "html",
            "source": "<div class=\"grid\">\n  <article class=\"g-col-6 g-start-4 md:g-col-4 md:g-start-5\">Centered content</article>\n</div>"
          }
        ],
        "paragraphs": [
          "With the default twelve columns, spans range from 1 through 12 and starts from 1 through 11. A start-only item has auto end placement. The grid-column shorthand used by g-col resets an earlier start to auto; repeat the start at the same responsive tier when it must persist. Generated CSS order, not HTML class order, determines conflicts.",
          "Items wrap when the remaining tracks cannot fit their span. A start plus span beyond the configured count can create implicit tracks. Runtime column tokens change track count but do not regenerate or clamp literal placement classes."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Containment and intrinsic sizing",
        "paragraphs": [
          "Each grid establishes inline-size containment. Give shrink-to-fit or auto-track layouts an appropriate inline size or minimum, and test long content, zoom, RTL and overflow. Plain 1fr tracks retain their automatic minimum; constrain or wrap oversized content deliberately.",
          "There are no legacy child-span classes or alternate fallback tokens in the strict core. For a nested layout, each grid redeclares its own column, row and gap defaults, and its descendants query that nested container. A container cannot query itself."
        ]
      },
      {
        "heading": "Nesting",
        "code": [
          {
            "language": "html",

          "headings": [
            "Token",
            "Default"
          ],

            [

              "Sass grid-columns (12)"

This entry does not include Reboot, components, color palettes or general helpers. Supply application-wide reset and theme styles separately when required.",
          "For Sass, configure tremplin/scss/config before loading tremplin/scss/tremplin-grid. The focused entry forwards the utilities map, not shared configuration options. Do not combine full and focused Sass entries in one compilation: loading Grid first filters shared utilities, while loading the full entry first causes a banner configuration error. This is a pinned upstream limitation; choose one entry per stylesheet."
